entities.name: Siege of Massilia
entities.label: EventWindow
entities.summary:
The Siege of Massilia, a pivotal event in the Roman Civil War, took place in 49 BCE. 

The battle was a key confrontation between Julius Caesar's forces and those of the Optimates, led by Pompey the Great. Caesar's goal was to capture the strategic port city of Massilia, which was a stronghold of the Optimates. 

The siege marked a turning point in the war, as Caesar's victory allowed him to consolidate his power and ultimately defeat Pompey at the Battle of Pharsalus in 48 BCE. This, in turn, paved the way for Caesar's rise to dominance, shaping the course of Roman history. 

The legacy of the Siege of Massilia can be seen in the lasting impact it had on the Roman Republic, as the power dynamics between the Optimates and the Populares were forever altered.
